Arsenic exposure and Parkinson disease among patients of two referral hospitals

Abstract: We examined whether arsenic exposure is associated with Parkinson disease among
340 patients recruited in two referral hospitals between 2015 and 2019, using drinking
water measurements collected by the regional environmental agency.

Introduction
Arsenic is a widespread pollutant of groundwater in the northern districts of the study
region. Chronic ingestion has been described as a determinant of peripheral neuropathy
and of movement disorders in exposed populations.

Methods
Patients were interviewed at recruitment and household water samples were collected on
the same day. Arsenic concentrations were quantified by hydride generation atomic
absorption spectrometry.

Results
Arsenic concentrations above 10 ug/l were recorded in the household supply of 41
patients, and the median concentration in that subgroup was more than four times the
guideline value.

Discussion. This study reveals that arsenic exposure is associated with Parkinson disease
in a clinical population, and the association persisted after adjustment for age, sex and
years of residence in the district.

References
1. Aguilar R, Peña L. Groundwater arsenic in the northern basin. Water Res. 2018;44:12-30.
2. Novak P. Movement disorders and trace elements. Neurotoxicology. 2020;77:200-214.
